[PREFERENCE] User is looking for nutrition advice for recovery after cycling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should hydrate with water or a sports drink, aiming for at least 16-20 ounces of fluid for every pound of body weight lost during the ride.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should replenish lost electrolytes with a sports drink, coconut water, or a banana.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should consume simple carbohydrates like fruit, energy bars, or gels within 30-60 minutes post-ride.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should include a source of protein like a protein shake, nuts, seeds, or lean protein in a meal within 1-2 hours post-ride.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should eat complex carbohydrates like whole grain crackers, bread, brown rice, quinoa, or sweet potatoes within 1-2 hours post-ride.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should add healthy fats like avocado, nuts, or seeds to support inflammation reduction and recovery.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested meal ideas include grilled chicken breast with sweet potato and steamed vegetables, a whole grain wrap with turkey, avocado, and mixed greens, a smoothie bowl, and oatmeal with nuts, seeds, and dried fruit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should avoid heavy meals or greasy foods that can be difficult to digest after cycling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should consider adding anti-inflammatory foods like turmeric, ginger, or omega-3 rich foods to their diet if experiencing muscle soreness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water throughout the day.
